maria: Heads up — after the kv-paging refactor I'm seeing intermittent 99p tail latency spikes on long-context jobs (30k+ tokens). Not steady, maybe every few minutes :thinking_face:
chen: Which workload? any repro or logs?
maria: Mainly the streaming chatbench run (multi-session, history reuse). Repro is flaky but I grabbed a perf trace and heap snapshot.
maria: Profiling snippet (hotspots):
```
kv_reuse_check  42%  (lock wait + manual evict path)
fifo_reinsert   18%  (memory copy + index update)
page_scan       15%  (compact/fragments)
rpc_serialize   8%
other           17%
```
sam: Huh. That `lock wait + manual evict path` ring a bell — could be reinserts fighting eviction under bursty multi-session reuse. Are we seeing reinsert of partially-evicted pages?
maria: Exactly my thought. When a session's prefix gets paged, request A evicts a chunk, request B then re-populates a subset, we end up chasing small fragments and doing repeated copy/allocs. Latency blips correlate with GC and memcpy spikes.
raul: Do you have the exact config used? batch sizes, eviction watermark, LRU window?
maria: Config excerpt: `kv.eviction_policy: fifo`, `kv.fifo.max_in_flight_reinserts: 8`, `kv.page_watermark: 75%`, streaming batch target `tokens_per_batch: 64`.
chen: Interesting you set fifo. With FIFO we can get pathological reinserts if many short-lived contexts push older pages out even though they're hot for other sessions. LRU would prefer reuse but is heavier to update.
sam: We changed kernel scheduling recently too — could be a timing interaction where batching/kernels delay reinserts and cause a reordering that FIFO hates.
raul: Can you paste the small stack dump around the high-latency sample?
maria: Stack (trimmed):
```
#0  kv_fifo_reinsert (kv.c:482)
#1  kv_insert_fragment (kv.c:351) 
#2  runtime_handle_request (serve.c:1203)
#3  batch_scheduler_wait_and_dispatch (batch.c:678)
#4  process_stream (stream.c:243)
```
ops-bot: deploy-bot noticed a config roll 1768887901 -> kv.fifo.max_in_flight_reinserts=8 (by @deploybot) :information_source:
chen: Good catch — the deploy changed the default from 16 -> 8 yesterday. Lower in-flight reinserts reduces memory pressure but increases reinsert churn.
sam: Hypothesis: lower in-flight reinserts + FIFO causes many small fragments to be reinserted synchronously, holding the kv lock and blocking other reqs -> tail spikes.
raul: Quick experiments we can do: 1) switch policy to LRU on a canary pool 2) bump fifo.max_in_flight_reinserts back to 16 3) enable fragment coalescing in the pager (cheap compaction pass)
maria: I tried bumping to 16 on a dev pool earlier today — fewer spikes in 30m run. But we need to be careful: LRU reduces cycles but increases update cost on hot paths.
chen: Could also try hybrid approach: FIFO overall but per-session LRU queues for recent hits. Less lock contention if we do per-worker mini-LRU and occasional merge.
sam: Agreed. Also add metrics: `kv.fragment_count`, `kv.reinsert_per_sec`, `kv.lock_hold_ms_p50/p95` so we can correlate.
maria: Created a quick dashboard and a short-term alert (p95 > 200ms) — will share link in a follow-up.
raul: Can you open a ticket with a short repro recipe and attach trace + heap? I'll pair on the patch.
maria: Ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-2345 (repro: chatbench long-history, set fifo.max_in_flight_reinserts=8, run for 10m). Attached perf trace and heap.
chen: For the canary: I'll spin up a pool with `kv.eviction_policy=lru` + `kv.fifo.max_in_flight_reinserts=16` and run the 2-hour smoke.
sam: If LRU fixes it, we'll need microbench for update cost (hot path) and consider an adaptive window. Also test with kernel scheduling changes (recent PR #2106).
maria: Action items:
- chen: canary LRU pool + 2h smoke (ETA 2h)
- raul/maria: draft light-weight fragment coalescer (PR)
- sam: add metrics and p95 alert
- ops-bot: rollback kv.fifo.max_in_flight_reinserts to 16 on prod if spikes continue
ops-bot: scheduled rollback (manual) window at 1768892000 if triggered :rotating_light:
chen: noted. I'll post results and attach flamegraphs.
maria: Thanks team. Will update ticket with canary logs. :thumbsup:
